items.body:
## Summary

During an active voice conversation, I asked the assistant to communicate with my existing text conversation so that work agreed during the call could continue there. Instead, the voice assistant attempts `dot.notify_parent` and reports that it has no associated parent. The requested message never reaches the text conversation.

The requested destination is the other user-facing conversation, not a parent agent. The text assistant incorrectly described itself as the voice thread's parent during troubleshooting. That relationship was not verified and should not be assumed. The user intends communication between the voice and text threads (described by the user as sibling threads), not a notification to an orchestration parent.

This report concerns the active voice-call handoff, not ordinary cloud coding tasks or an audio-development task with a similar name.

## Steps to reproduce (user-reported)

1. Start a voice call with the assistant while an existing text conversation is available.
2. Ask voice to send agreed work or a simple identifying message to that text conversation.
3. Voice attempts `dot.notify_parent` and reports that its thread has no associated parent.
4. Check the text conversation: the requested message does not arrive.

## Expected behavior

Provide a supported, appropriately scoped route between the user's voice and text conversations. Resolve and verify the intended destination rather than assuming that the other conversation is a parent. A parent-notification method must not be substituted for a requested cross-thread message when that relationship does not exist.

If this communication is unsupported, explain that accurately rather than repeatedly attempting the wrong route or claiming an unverified parent relationship. The user should not have to manually relay all the work discussed during a call.

## Actual behavior and impact

The handoff stalls. Work agreed in voice is not transferred to the text conversation. The user must repeat instructions, relay details manually, and troubleshoot thread identifiers. Listing unrelated cloud tasks does not identify or resolve the active voice session.

## Evidence and limits

- Observed on October 20, 2026, with the text conversation open on Windows/web while voice was active.
- The method name and missing-parent condition are reported by the user from the voice interaction; an exact raw error payload and voice-side execution trace are not available here.
- No requested handoff was received in the text conversation. This establishes missing delivery, not the underlying implementation cause or actual thread topology.
- App/build version and voice-client platform were not captured.
- No private conversation contents, account identifiers, or thread IDs are included.

Related context: #41706 concerns parent-bound return channels for separately created tasks. This report is different: the user needs voice-to-text cross-thread communication, and the intended recipient must not be assumed to be a parent. Please route to the appropriate voice/integration component if maintained outside this repository.

## Why

Reducing code cell lifecycle events discarded their response payload references and lost the initial response status when the runtime status changed.

Extend lifecycle tests to verify distinct initial and final payload IDs and the preserved initial status for yielded cells that complete and failed cells whose lifecycle events precede their source item.

items.title: Share prepared MCP tool definitions across sessions
items.body:
Share prepared MCP tool definitions across sessions

## Why

Sessions using the same MCP catalog can repeat schema normalization and retain duplicate tool specifications.

## What changed

Split immutable MCP tool metadata and normalized specifications from per-handler caches, and reuse matching definitions within each `McpManager`. Require matching tool metadata, agent-plugin mode, and schema budget before reuse.

Keep shared definitions behind weak references and prune expired entries on cache misses so completed sessions do not keep their schemas alive. Build definitions outside the shared index lock.

items.title: Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications
items.body:
Avoid redundant clones when sending app-server notifications

## Why

Targeted notification delivery and broadcast routing clone the message for every recipient, then discard the original.

## What changed

Use `std::iter::repeat_n` to move the original message to the last recipient, avoiding one clone per nonempty recipient list while preserving delivery behavior.

## Testing

Expand notification tests to cover empty, single, and multiple recipient lists, checking payloads, target order, and shared timestamps. Add broadcast coverage for zero, one, and two eligible recipients, verifying that uninitialized clients, clients without the required experimental API support, and clients that opted out are skipped.

items.title: [macOS Desktop 26.1013.40934] Follow-up stays queued while thread is idle; replying in another window releases it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### App version

macOS desktop bundle `com.openai.codex`: **26.1013.40934**, build **20770**, verified from the installed application. The updater reported up to date during diagnosis.

### Subscription and platform

ChatGPT account; subscription tier and exact macOS release were not collected for this report. The affected Codex chat runs locally on the Mac and uses a custom study plugin backed by an MCP service.

### What happened?

A follow-up remains above the composer with a spinning queued/Sending indicator after the preceding response has completed. Read-only thread inspection reports **idle**, the prior turn completed, and **no next turn**. The user confirmed the affected chat was open in a **separate study window**.

This recurred after an application reconnect/restart allowed one successful exchange. Later, the user replied in a different troubleshooting chat in the main window; the stalled study chat then began working. Logs correlate that other-chat submission with dispatch of the stalled study turn **5.922 seconds later**.

This report concerns a dispatch stall before model/MCP execution, not merely a stale pending indicator after successful execution. The precise cause remains unconfirmed.

### Observed sequence

Intermittent incident sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Use an existing local chat in a separate desktop window while another chat is available in the main window.
2. Complete a normal exchange that includes an MCP save and a final assistant response.
3. Submit the next answer. It remains queued/spinning above the composer. Thread inspection still reports idle with no corresponding new turn.
4. In the observed recovery, reply in the other chat in the main window.
5. The main window dispatches the stalled chat's turn about six seconds later. Pending work completes.

The user did not report moving the study chat into the main window or completing the proposed single-window/manual-Send test. We therefore do not claim either as a verified workaround.

### Redacted timeline and diagnostics

All timestamps below are **2026-10-21 UTC**:

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 01:08:03–01:08:34 | Prior study turn completed normally. Progress read: 1,381 ms; one save: **153 ms**; no save retry. |
| During the stall | Repeated thread reads showed idle and no next turn despite the user-visible pending message. |
| 01:24:25 | The user's other-chat reply started from the focused main window. |
| 01:24:31 | That same window dispatched the stalled study turn, **5.922 seconds later**. |
| 01:24:31–01:24:39 | Resumed turn acknowledged an already-saved answer without saving it again. |
| 01:24:39–01:25:01 | Following turn completed, with one progress read (1,383 ms) and one save (**151 ms**). Independent application readback validated the receipt chain and one additional saved record. |

Window logs show the focused study view as a **follower**, while another window dispatched successful turns. Owner identities alternated at turn start and completion. Queue activity resumed across three windows during recovery; the separate study window remained a follower. This supports investigating window/focus coordination, but does not prove an ownership repair or a causal mechanism.

A nearby warning was:

```text
[IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured
method=thread-queued-followups-changed
```

The warning contains no thread ID and also appeared around successful submissions, so it is **not evidence by itself of the root cause**.

### Expected behaviour

When a local thread is idle, sending its next message should start exactly one turn, independent of activity in another desktop window. If dispatch cannot proceed, preserve the input and show an actionable status rather than an indefinite spinner.

### Troubleshooting and limits

- An earlier, separate plugin issue synchronously waited for reader publication during saves. That was repaired before this recurrence; the measured completed saves returned in 153 and 151 ms.
- Installed plugin source/cache integrity was verified. No evidence establishes the plugin as the cause of this desktop dispatch stall.
- Changing Queue to Steer was not treated as a repair: those settings govern input during an active run, whereas this thread was idle.
- No internal app database or settings were edited, no learner messages were replayed by diagnostic tooling, and no permanent client fix is claimed.
- Raw logs, screenshots, prompts, personal filesystem paths, hostnames, account/session IDs and learner records are omitted from this public report.

### Related reports

Possibly related, without asserting a shared root cause:

- #49456 — accepted input remains queued with follower/owner-state inconsistencies. This incident instead had no new turn until recovery.
- #51251 — queued/Steer messages intermittently fail to dispatch without a visible error, observed during an active run.

Please consolidate with an existing engineering issue if appropriate.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### Codex version and platform

Codex CLI and managed app-server 0.163.0 on Linux. The same behavior was reproduced with the local daemon and `--remote unix://`.

### Reproduction

1. Start an existing interactive thread on `gpt-5.6-sol` with `medium` reasoning.
2. While that thread is active, queue a follow-up for the same thread:

   ```console
   codex queue --thread <thread-uuid> --model gpt-6-sol --message 'Continue with the next task'
   ```

3. Let the queued follow-up start its own turn and inspect the new turn's effective model/effort (`/status` or persisted `turn_context`).

### Expected

The follow-up turn uses `gpt-6-sol` with `medium` reasoning, or the CLI rejects `--model` as unsupported rather than accepting and silently ignoring it.

### Actual

The command reports that the message was queued. The next turn in the same thread still records `gpt-5.6-sol` / `medium`. Adding `--remote unix://` and `-c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"'` did not change this.

### Root-cause evidence

In tag `rust-v0.163.0`, [`queue_cmd.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/cli/src/queue_cmd.rs) accepts the flattened interactive flags, including `--model`. [`session_queue_commands.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/tui/src/session_queue_commands.rs) sends only `threadId`, message `input`, and `clientUserMessageId` to `thread/queue/add`. [`ThreadQueueAddParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs) contains no model or effort fields, and the queue processor enqueues only the input. Current upstream `main` still has this request shape as of this report.

A separate local app-server `thread/settings/update` before queuing was able to set the thread's next-turn model and effort, and the next persisted turn recorded the requested pair. That is a version-specific workaround, not a repair to `codex queue --model` or per-message queue semantics.

Related but broader desktop UI request: #50383. This report is the CLI's accepted-but-ignored `--model` option for an existing thread.

No thread IDs, credentials, or private logs are included.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex desktop app and mobile Remote. The requested interaction model should also work consistently across supported CLI and IDE clients.

### What feature would you like to see?

## Summary

Please let multiple authorized devices remain connected to the **same live Codex thread** and submit text, photos, screenshots, file attachments, and follow-up requests while **one execution agent remains responsible for the session**.

Request submission should not require taking over execution ownership or acquiring and retaining the thread's exclusive writer lock. Requests should enter one shared, ordered queue, synchronize across clients, and be processed by the existing executor at appropriate safe checkpoints.

This is a request for **multiple input clients with one executor**, not parallel execution by multiple agents.

## Why this matters to my workflow

My workflow is to keep Codex working on my computer while I use my phone or another device to review progress and add information or instructions to that same conversation. A photo, attachment, clarification, or change of direction can become relevant while the computer is still working.

The current ownership/access friction disrupts this way of working. I should not have to return to the computer, close the original session, or fork the conversation merely to deliver another request. Read-only access helps with monitoring, but does not satisfy the need to contribute to the ongoing work.

**Please treat this as a core multi-device workflow issue that deserves explicit attention and a reliable product-level solution.** For users who work this way, dependable participation from another device is fundamental to the usefulness of Remote, rather than an occasional convenience.

OpenAI's [Remote engineering guide](https://developers.openai.com/blog/mastering-codex-remote-for-engineering) already describes mobile steering, queued prompts, and attachments. The request here is to make those capabilities dependable when multiple supported clients remain attached to the same active session.

## Requested behavior

1. **Simultaneous access to the same thread.** Authorized devices can view the conversation, live progress, pending requests, and outcomes without closing another client or creating a separate conversation.

2. **Separate request submission from execution ownership.** A client submits a request to the existing session and receives an acknowledgement and request ID. It does not become another executor or hold exclusive session ownership while waiting. The existing executor retains the protections needed to serialize execution and history updates.

3. **One authoritative request order.** Requests from all devices enter the same queue, ordered by server acceptance by default, with that order visible everywhere. Retries and reconnections should deduplicate the same submission rather than enqueue it twice. Distinguish an unsent local draft from a request acknowledged by the session.

4. **Safe processing without rejecting ordinary input because the executor is busy.** Process steering requests at the next supported safe checkpoint and normal follow-ups at the appropriate turn boundary. During an operation that cannot safely be interrupted, continue accepting and queuing requests, then process them when safe. Show why they are waiting. Acceptance into the queue must not imply immediate execution or permission to interrupt a protected operation.

5. **First-class attachments.** Transfer the actual photo/file content, or a resolvable attachment reference, to the execution host. Keep it associated with its request across queueing and reconnection. A sender-local file path alone is insufficient; upload failures must be visible and must not silently produce an incomplete executable request.

6. **Visible request lifecycle and recovery.** Show states such as uploading, queued, waiting for a safe checkpoint, processing, completed, failed, and cancelled. Clearly distinguish delivery acknowledgement from agent consumption and completion, and associate the result with the request. Allow cancellation before processing and safe retry after a delivery failure without losing text or attachments.

7. **Optional priority.** Allow an explicit priority for pending requests, with any resulting order change synchronized across clients. Priority must not bypass safe checkpoints, required approvals, or an operation already in progress. FIFO can be the initial implementation.

## Ownership and implementation boundaries

Preserve the single-writer invariant. The requested change is how clients submit input to the owner, not removal of persistence locks or permission for independent runtimes to modify the same thread.

A shared app-server or forwarding requests to the current owner could satisfy this model; the implementation is up to the maintainers. An executor may legitimately retain ownership for the lifetime of a live session. Input clients should not need to compete for that ownership.

The initial scope can be one user's authorized devices with the execution host online. Multi-user collaboration, host migration, and parallel agents are not prerequisites.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Leave a desktop task running and open the same thread on a phone without closing the desktop session.
- Submit a photo and instruction from the phone, then another request from the desktop. Both clients show the same accepted requests and authoritative queue order.
- Verify that only the existing execution agent processes those requests and that the attachments are readable on the execution host.
- During a non-interruptible operation, new requests remain accepted and visibly queued; they are processed at a safe boundary without terminating that operation.
- Disconnect and reconnect a client after acknowledgement. The accepted request, attachments, state, and outcome remain available without duplicate submission.
- Both clients converge on the same conversation and request states without restarting the application.

### Additional information

## Related reports and overlap

I reviewed existing reports before opening this request. There is substantial overlap in the overall goal, and these reports should inform a shared solution:

- [#40558](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40558): active desktop threads are listed on iOS but fail to load because of an active-writer conflict. Comments also describe blocked follow-up instructions and the need to leave the desktop/IDE open.
- [#37403, maintainer explanation](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37403#issuecomment-5496797894): explains why separate writers can corrupt history and describes multiple clients interacting with one live session through a shared app-server. This proposal preserves that invariant.
- [#33948](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33948) and [#40124](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40124): request live session continuity across devices and returning to the same CLI/mobile session with context intact.
- [#27565](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/27565): requests bidirectional real-time messaging between terminal and mobile clients.
- [#29094](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/29094): reports mobile turns not appearing live in the desktop view.
- [#35759](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35759): an adjacent cross-host workflow demonstrates why attachment delivery must carry usable content rather than sender-local paths.
- [#55200](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55200): reports stale desktop activity and stuck queued messages during Windows/Android use, with requests for queue visibility and non-disruptive reconnection.

These reports do not establish a single shared root cause, and I am not claiming to have independently reproduced all of them. The focused addition here is an explicit behavioral contract for **simultaneous multi-device request submission, one executor, ordered and acknowledged delivery, safe processing, and synchronized request status**.

If an existing issue is the intended umbrella for this complete workflow, please link or consolidate this proposal there while retaining these acceptance criteria.

review. A receipt for commentary must never admit final. Missing review, wrong

without an external user saying continue. Preserve explicit Owner stop, existing
tool/permission gates and legitimate WAIT. A background polling monitor is not an
acceptable substitute.

   A later review cannot retroactively protect that first display.

   assistant text can omit the helper; Stop occurs after output.

Primary source #47679 implements ModelRequestContributor/ModelResponseInterceptor,
including buffering before core response delivery. Its registry accepts typed
Rust Arc trait implementations and produces an immutable registry. Current public
app-server/src/extensions.rs installs compiled contributors in thread_extensions.

hot-load interface in the installed Desktop.

safe attachment contract. The installed experimental client protocol inspection

The affected user explicitly requested this bug report. The observed mismatch is confirmed; the underlying cause is not established.

- Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0` (read with `Get-AppxPackage`; not an About-dialog version).

- Tool: `mcp__cua_repl`.
- Fresh direct access check: October 21, 2026, Europe/Madrid.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Default | Always allow | Requires approval |
| `https://secure.arsys.es` | Always allow | Requires approval |

The screenshot also shows an allowance for `https://pdc.arsys.es`. No download was requested by the failing call, so the separate download approval setting is not the operation being exercised.

The original screenshot is not attached here because it includes unrelated site entries. No claim is made that all possible organization/device policies have been audited.

## Reproduction observed in the affected session

1. Start a fresh documented CUA session after the previous automation session had been reset.
2. `await cua.getState()` succeeds and lists the connected Google Chrome browser.
3. Select that browser with `cua.getBrowser(...)`; setup and documentation succeed.

```js
await browser.nameSession("Arsys access check");
await cua.createBrowserTab(browser.browserId, "https://secure.arsys.es/", {
  sessionName: "Arsys access check"
});
```

6. The user provides the screenshot showing the exact-origin navigation allowance.

A fresh CUA session is not a clean-profile or full-app-restart test. No such test is claimed in this report.

## Actual result (verbatim)

```text
Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: A saved user permission setting blocks this action. Browser use could not acquire authority to trigger network egress. The origin approval gate did not grant access for https://secure.arsys.es. A saved permission or managed policy denies access. The agent must not attempt to achieve the same outcome via workaround, indirect execution, raw CDP or browser commands, alternate browser surfaces, or policy circumvention. Proceed only with a materially safer alternative that does not require this blocked browser action; if none exists, stop and request user input.
```

This does not establish an Arsys HTTP error, failed login, or incorrect user configuration: no provider page was reached by this call.

- An exact-origin navigation allowance should be reflected in the effective permission decision, unless a legitimate overriding restriction applies.
- If an overriding restriction applies, identify its source and provide a supported recovery path, rather than only attributing the decision to a saved permission that conflicts with the visible UI.
- Please investigate the permission-state/UI mismatch on this Windows app version and document a supported way to reconcile the effective decision with the user's explicit allowance.
- This is not a request to bypass or weaken browser security.

The refusal blocks authorized hosting administration needed to complete a current private WordPress backup. No hosting changes were made as part of this access check.

No workaround was attempted after the denial. No permission files were edited. No raw browser protocol, alternate browser surface, direct request to the blocked origin, or credential extraction was used. The automation session was released afterward.

No credentials, cookies, account email, private chat/session IDs, full transcripts, local filesystem paths, hosting contents, or database backups are included.

## Related reports

- #50640 describes a closely matching Windows Chrome permission/UI mismatch on an earlier Windows package, including a per-chat deny observed in that separate report.
- #55675 reports a similar symptom in the Windows built-in browser.

These establish related symptoms, not a verified shared root cause. This report adds a current Windows Chrome observation on package `26.1013.4894.0`, with the exact-origin allowance visible and a navigation-only request rejected. Please link or consolidate as appropriate.

After the original submission, the user explicitly reported restarting Codex. A new documented CUA setup and a direct Chrome new-tab navigation to the same exact HTTPS origin returned the identical origin-approval denial before page content was returned.

The user then explicitly reported restarting Chrome as well. The fresh browser inventory showed a new Chrome connection with only a new-tab page. The restarts are reported by the user; the new Chrome connection and both subsequent rejections were directly observed by the agent. This is not a clean-profile or clean-install test. No alternative surface, direct network workaround, policy-file edit, or hosting modification was attempted.

The user subsequently opened the Arsys Client Area manually and explicitly asked the agent to inspect that existing tab. The browser inventory listed the tab, but the normal documented `cua.getTab(...)` operation was rejected as well. This rejection says **"Browser use could not acquire authority to observe page content"**, with the same exact-origin approval denial. Only create dispatch-based `write_stdin` terminal operations for calls without a namespace.

Add replay regression coverage for prefixed and unprefixed MCP aliases, names that match built-in tools, and `write_stdin` arguments with and without a session ID. labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.163.0

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to terminal input handling.

### Which model were you using?

Not model-dependent.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0

Native Windows Codex, not WSL. The same keys work under WSL.

### Codex doctor report

Not collected. The failure is in the keyboard-event parser Codex pins.

### What issue are you seeing?

With a Russian or Armenian keyboard layout active, Ctrl+C is not recognized by the Codex TUI on
Windows. Ctrl+D, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and the other Ctrl+letter shortcuts fail the same way. Switching
to an English layout makes them work again.

Windows delivers Ctrl+C as a console key record whose character is the control code 0x03. The
pinned crossterm (`openai-oss-forks/crossterm@ed1cdab`) sends every control code through
`get_char_for_key`, which looks the key up in the active layout with no modifiers. Under a
non-Latin layout that returns the layout's character or nothing, so no binding matches. A probe
that prints crossterm's `event::read()` recorded these Ctrl+C presses:

| Layout   | Reported by the pinned crossterm | Reported with the fix   |
| -------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| English  | `Char('c')` + `CONTROL`          | `Char('c')` + `CONTROL` |
| Russian  | no event                         | `Char('c')` + `CONTROL` |
| Armenian | `Char('ց')` (U+0581) + `CONTROL` | `Char('c')` + `CONTROL` |

This is the Windows counterpart of #35599, which covers the same symptom from the kitty keyboard
protocol on Linux and macOS. The two paths are separate: #35599 needs the base-layout key from
crossterm#1074, and this one is fixed in crossterm's Windows parser.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, add a Russian keyboard layout and switch to it.
2. Run `codex`.
3. Press Ctrl+C, or Ctrl+D with an empty composer.
4. Nothing happens. With an English layout, the same keys show the quit hint or quit.

At the parser level: a key record with `u_char = 0x03`, `LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED` and virtual key
`0x43` is looked up in the active layout instead of being reported as Ctrl+C.

### What is the expected behavior?

Ctrl+letter shortcuts work whatever keyboard layout is active, as they do on an English layout
and under WSL.

### Additional information

Fix in crossterm: https://github.com/crossterm-rs/crossterm/pull/1156

When Ctrl is held without Alt, the parser reports Ctrl+A to Ctrl+Z by their control codes
(0x01..=0x1a) instead of going through the layout lookup. Armenian sends Ctrl+Shift+letter with
no character, so for those records the letter comes from the virtual key.

The table above comes from a probe built on the pinned crossterm before and after the fix. A Codex
build with the patched crossterm was also checked by hand under the Russian and Armenian layouts.
For Codex, the change is a crossterm pin bump in `codex-rs/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and
`MODULE.bazel.lock` once the fork includes it.

- The problem also appears in direct-command and browser results outside code mode

## Summary

On Windows, the built-in browser rejects access to `https://www.nexusmods.com` as denied by a saved user permission, while the desktop Browser settings visibly show **Always allow** for Browsing and Downloads on the Nexus site entry. Repeated attempts still fail after resetting the site exception and completely restarting the desktop app.

Submitted at the affected user's explicit request. This is an observed session report, not an independently reproduced clean-install test.

## Environment

- Windows version/build reported locally: 10.0.26200.0.
- Installed package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0 (Windows package metadata).
- Desktop UI identifies itself as ChatGPT; local Work/Codex task.
- Browser surface: built-in browser (`iab`).
- Tool: `mcp__cua_repl`.
- Observed: October 20, 2026, America/Chicago.

## Reproduction and evidence

1. Open Settings > Browser > Website permissions.
2. Allow Browsing and Downloads for the Nexus HTTPS site entry. User-supplied screenshots were inspected and show both set to Always allow, plus a separate allowed Nexus file-CDN entry.
3. Ask the agent to open:
   `https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/64445?tab=files`
4. The documented browser call is:
   ```js
   await cua.createBrowserTab('iab',
     'https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/64445?tab=files',
     {visible:true});
   ```
5. The tool rejects the navigation before page content is returned.
6. The user removed/re-added the exception, requested retests, and later explicitly confirmed a complete desktop-app restart. The same error persisted.
7. The user can manually open Nexus in the built-in browser; ambient UI context reports a tab at `https://www.nexusmods.com/`. Manual visibility does not establish agent authorization.

## Actual result

```text
Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy.
Reason: A saved user permission setting blocks this action.
Browser use could not acquire authority to trigger network egress.
The origin approval gate did not grant access for https://www.nexusmods.com.
A saved permission or managed policy denies access.
```

No saved denial was manually confirmed in underlying permission files. A stale per-session denial, a higher-priority policy, or a UI/runtime mismatch are possible explanations; the precise cause is unverified. The user reports not intentionally denying access.

The effective browser permission should reflect the user's explicit site allowance, or the app should identify the overriding restriction and provide a supported recovery action. Please investigate why the visible allow setting and rejection disagree, and how the user can revoke an effective saved denial through the supported UI.

Potentially related: #50640 (Windows Chrome, including per-session deny evidence), #49453, and #50789 (macOS). This report concerns the **built-in browser on Windows** and does not assume their root cause.

No workaround was attempted following the policy rejection. No credentials, cookies, account identifiers, private chat IDs, full session logs, or desktop screenshots are attached. Screenshots were replaced by the relevant setting values in this report.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

26.1013.31256, build 20586, macOS desktop. Resolver asset: `app-initial-3ccf4886957f.js`.
The separate read-only catalog diagnostic used codex-cli 0.153.4.

### What subscription do you have?

Account/subscription details omitted. This reproduction concerns account-scoped MCP Apps routing.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Apple Silicon.

### What issue are you seeing?

A model-initiated Uno read succeeds using a secondary connected account. Its MCP Apps card renders the committed Kit. Clicking **Refresh** consistently fails with:

```
Unable to refresh. Try again.
```

The desktop host log gives the actual rejection:

```
errorCode=-32603
errorMessage="MCP app cannot call tool outside its trusted tool scope: uno_show_kit"
method=tools/call
server=codex_apps
```

The error repeats on a fresh card. It occurs before dispatch to Uno. Direct authenticated reads using the secondary account continue to succeed with the original commit unchanged.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Connect Primary and a secondary account to the same registered MCP integration.
2. Invoke its read-only card tool as the secondary account.
3. In the card, call that same raw server tool through MCP Apps `tools/call`.
4. Observe the host trusted-tool-scope rejection, even though the initial model tool call worked.

#### Captured catalog shape and source-level reproduction

The authenticated `mcpServerStatus/list` catalog merges Uno accounts into one descriptor:

```json
{
  "name": "uno.uno_show_kit",
  "title": "uno_show_kit",
  "_meta": {
    "connector_id": "connector_example",
    "link_id": "link_primary",
    "_codex_apps": {
      "resource_uri": "/connector_example/link_primary/uno_show_kit",
      "contains_mcp_source": true,
      "requires_explicit_link_id": true
    },
    "link_accounts": [
      {"link_id": "link_primary"},
      {"link_id": "link_secondary"}
    ]
  }
}
```

Identifiers above are synthetic. In the installed resolver, tools are filtered against the trusted target **before** name resolution. Descriptor target identity comes from its default routing URI. The merged descriptor is therefore accepted for Primary and excluded for the secondary target despite that target being in `link_accounts`.

Replaying the extracted resolver with the captured catalog reproduces the rejection for both raw and namespaced tool names. Primary succeeds. Adding a tool-name prefix is insufficient.

The exact live card's cached scope object was not exported; the source-copy tests exercise the secondary target scope implied by its selected connection. Provider and network boundaries are mocked. This is a concrete resolver defect reproducing the observed error, not a claim that a patched production host has been verified.

### Patch proposal and automated regression evidence

[Sanitized reproduction, guarded patch proposal, tests, red/green results and source hash](https://gist.github.com/christopherwxyz/bcc26a6cd77810a8cc64f1bf9dff2d07).

Run on the matching desktop build:

```sh
python3 extract-host.py
BASELINE=1 node --test regression.cjs
node --test regression.cjs
```

Baseline: **8 pass, 8 fail**, including the exact reduced-app Refresh error. Candidate: **16 pass**.

The proposed host-boundary change:

- Materializes only a target listed by the authoritative catalog, within the same trusted connector.
- Requires consistent routing metadata, explicit-link support, and one unambiguous account match.
- Excludes synthetic descriptors; preserves existing policy, schema and file-parameter restrictions.
- Binds dispatch `link_id` to the trusted target and rejects conflicting account arguments before dispatch.
- Preserves connector-wide explicit-account behavior.

Tests cover selected-account dispatch metadata and arguments, Primary continuity, all listed targets, foreign connectors, unlisted accounts, ambiguous names, synthetic links, source descriptor immutability and read-only Refresh. Independent review identified synthetic-link and connector-scope edge cases; both have regression coverage.

The patch is a guarded source-copy proposal for maintainers to port to typed host source. Installed files are unchanged. The public bundle contains synthetic identifiers and a reduced UI; it excludes captured private connection metadata, raw logs, the private app HTML and vendor source. Source extraction runs locally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Refresh should call the read tool through the secondary account's existing authenticated connection. It should render the same committed content and reenable without another login. A card must not select Primary implicitly or override its trusted account through arguments.

### Additional information

- [OpenAI MCP Apps UI guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui) uses raw tool names in `tools/call` examples.
- [Multi-account authentication guidance](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth#support-multiple-accounts) associates credentials with the selected connection.
- Similar rejection text appears in #50055 and #29210. Those reports do not establish this same merged-account cause.
- This is separate from browser automation navigation issue #55659. It does not concern iframe fetch timing or Cloudflare latency.

Production acceptance remains blocked pending a fixed host build. Please validate metadata authority, scope construction, catalog-refresh races, transport authorization, and both selected-account success and cross-account refusal when applying the fix.

items.body:
## Disposition: closing this overlapping umbrella request

I should have checked the existing reports before opening this issue. The fail-closed tool-policy requirement is already tracked in #41979; pre-render response holding is tracked in #43254. #54806 independently reports trusted hook discovery without effective Desktop interception on the same Windows backend version, including control-socket error 10050. #54427 tracks trusted resolved execution context, and #54872 covers cancellation-driven policy-gate waiting.

This report combined those requirements rather than isolating a demonstrated new defect. Closing in favor of the established reports. The local failed control is retained below as bounded evidence; its cause is unknown and it does not prove the same root cause as #54806. No working live-enforcement solution or maintainer acceptance is claimed. Any remaining user-conversation role-binding gap needs a separate novelty check before another report.

---

# Required native alignment admission is unavailable; hook failures cannot establish mandatory enforcement

For OpenAI Codex desktop/native runtime maintainers. Submitted with the reporter’s authorization.

## Requested outcome

Provide a host-owned, mandatory admission boundary before native actions and final rendering. The client needs to reject an action when required authority or a valid policy decision is unavailable. Optional repository adapters and additional prompt instructions cannot intercept paths that bypass them.

This request concerns deterministic action-policy enforcement. Delivery of instruction bytes does not prove that a model followed every instruction or reasoned correctly.

## Environment

- Windows; running desktop backend reports `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`.
- The PATH CLI reports `0.149.1`; it was not used for the fresh native probe.
- Node 24 with native TypeScript stripping. The intercepted probe target is the read-only local function `get_goal({})`, not a shell action.
- Probe runtime home, state, logs and temporary output are isolated beneath a repository-owned temporary fixture. Native turn context records approval `never` and sandbox `read-only`. This is configuration/path isolation, not a claim of OS-enforced confinement.

## Fresh observation, 2026-10-20

1. Discover a session-only `PreToolUse` command hook matching exactly `^get_goal$`.
2. Use only the host-returned hook key/hash to configure trust for the isolated child session.
3. Verify that the expected hook is trusted and enabled, with no other active trusted handler.
4. Emit exactly one `get_goal({})` call through a local deterministic Responses responder.
5. The native tool returns `goal: null`, but no matching hook-execution receipt is recorded. The control fails. Denial and failure cases are not run afterward.

The cause of this fresh missing receipt is not established. This result is not evidence of successful denial, successful interception, or current-chat enforcement.

A separate read-only attempt to connect to the existing app-server control socket failed with Windows socket error 10050. It created no thread and performed no configuration write. It does not establish that every possible host transport is unavailable.

## Prior bounded observations, 2026-10-19

A separately preserved assessment of the desktop backend version used the same non-shell target and matched native call/output records to hook receipts. A valid explicit denial blocked the call. Controlled exit 1, malformed hook output and timeout each allowed the call. These historical results have not been relabeled as fresh passing tests.

A custom Responses gateway separately withheld synthetic tool-call frames on negative/missing/invalid checks and gateway failures. That demonstrates only calls routed through that fixture gateway. No production upstream proxy, mandatory current-chat routing or global mediation was established.

## Documented constraints

[Official hook documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) describes supported explicit denial, callback failures that can leave actions unblocked, incomplete tool-path coverage, and exceptions to the ordinary hook path. [Plugin documentation](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) also requires separate trust for plugin hooks. Installing a plugin or catching errors inside a hook does not establish host-owned mandatory mediation.

## Smallest host-owned repair requested

1. Add an explicit required-policy admission contract, separate from ordinary advisory hooks. This is a proposed capability, not an existing setting.
2. Bind admission to the actual thread, turn, original outcome, exact operation/payload, authority revision and single-use request identity.
3. Enforce it at every relevant native dispatch path, including nested code-mode calls. Unsupported paths must be exposed and denied when required by policy, rather than silently bypassing admission.
4. Deny on missing/untrusted/modified authority, missing checker, launcher failure, checker crash, invalid response, deadline expiry or lost policy transport.
5. Apply the corresponding original-outcome gate before final bytes are rendered. Uncertain continuation effects must remain reserved across restart and require authoritative reconciliation.
6. Expose authenticated invocation/decision observations and a supported way to bind the current conversation. Caller-created environment secrets, local brands and authored JSON must not qualify as production host evidence.

Existing repository adapters already exercise sealed role/skill bodies, exact byte binding, issued guards, durable duplicate suppression and uncertain-effect reconciliation. They can be integration targets, but cannot establish their own mandatory invocation.

## Acceptance tests

- A positive exact-bound admission executes one harmless action once.
- Explicit denial and every unavailable/error path execute zero actions.
- Wrong-thread, wrong-turn, changed payload, changed authority, replay and expired admission are denied.
- Nested/local/MCP/subagent paths cannot bypass the required boundary; unsupported hosted paths are explicitly identified.
- An unfinished original outcome cannot release final bytes; continuation is acknowledged and duplicate-safe.
- Restart preserves reservations and original-parent identity.
- Tests inspect native dispatch and rendered-output evidence, not simulated assistant prose alone.

## Safety and disclosure

Persistent configuration, execution policy, signing-service/trust-authority work and native Stop enablement were excluded. Hashes of the three named configuration files match before/after the fresh probe; this is not a whole-host mutation audit. No production guard was installed. Private prompts, account information, credentials and conversation identifiers are intentionally excluded from this report.

## Separate project-hook role applicability defect

Source review found that a project-wide alignment command selected one assistant identity using only the repository working directory. Other role-specific conversations can share that directory. Matching source hashes and tests that assume a single role do not establish correct applicability. A reviewed inactive repository patch now emits only neutral workspace context and imports no role-specific memory/authority loader; it deliberately withholds role-specific context even in the intended assistant conversation until a trusted host identity exists. Prompt text, titles, transcript text, environment flags and caller-authored role fields cannot supply that identity.

Please expose a trustworthy role/session binding for user-owned conversations as well as native subagents, preserving it across resume and compaction. Optional subagent profile fields do not by themselves identify a separate user-owned conversation. This remains distinct from mandatory tool/final-render admission. No live configuration or trust change has been made.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

App

### What feature would you like to see?

Dear Codex Development Team,

I would like to suggest an improvement to the way Codex handles usage limits, particularly when working on larger software development projects.

I am currently developing an educational application with Codex. I find Codex extremely useful, but one of the most frustrating aspects is that usage limits can interrupt development tasks before they are completed.

As a user, I cannot reliably estimate how much of my available usage allowance a particular task will consume. Sometimes I can work for a long time on numerous small improvements, while a single larger task may exhaust my allowance surprisingly quickly.

This creates a particular problem when Codex has already started modifying an application. A task may be interrupted after some changes have been implemented but before testing, verification or deployment has been completed. This can leave the project in an uncertain or partially finished state.

My suggestion is to introduce a smart task queue with usage-aware task management.

Ideally, this would work as follows:

Users could queue a limited number of tasks, for example three at a time.

When one task is completed, another could be added to the queue.

Codex would estimate the expected resource requirements of queued tasks and compare them with the remaining usage allowance.

As the usage limit approaches, Codex would stop accepting new tasks.

Tasks that have already been accepted would be allowed to finish, including necessary testing and deployment, even if the normal limit for starting new tasks has been reached.

If completing all accepted tasks cannot be guaranteed, Codex should clearly indicate this before accepting them.

Before any unavoidable interruption, Codex should save the current development state, complete any necessary safety checks and provide a clear summary of completed and outstanding work.

I understand that accurately predicting the computational cost of a software development task is difficult and that completing accepted tasks might require a reserved resource allowance.

However, I believe there should be a clear distinction between stopping the acceptance of new tasks and interrupting tasks that are already in progress.

For users developing substantial applications, continuity and a reliable project state are extremely important.

I would much rather be told that Codex cannot accept another task until my allowance resets than have an existing task interrupted halfway through implementation.

This improvement would make Codex more predictable, reliable and practical for long-term software development, especially for users who are not professional software developers and cannot estimate the technical complexity of each request.

Thank you for considering this suggestion.

Kind regards Dagmar Pesta

26.1007.21434-win32-x64 (stable extension channel); bundled codex-cli reports 0.162.0-alpha.17.2

### What subscription do you have?

Company-managed ChatGPT account; exact subscription tier not specified.

### Which IDE are you using?

Visual Studio Code

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex fails to connect when VS Code inherits SSL_CERT_FILE from an Anaconda PowerShell, even though CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE is also set to a verified corporate root PEM. Removing only SSL_CERT_FILE from the launching shell makes Codex work while retaining the activated conda environment and CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE.

The machine uses corporate HTTPS inspection with CrowdStrike. The presented certificate for chatgpt.com has issuer O=CrowdStrike, CN=Falcon ROOT CA Proxy. The matching corporate root is trusted in Windows and exported to the PEM referenced by CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE. Anaconda points SSL_CERT_FILE at its Library\ssl\cacert.pem; that bundle was inspected and contains 121 certificates but no CrowdStrike root.

Browser authentication reports "Signed in to Codex", but VS Code reports "Sign-in failed: workspace routing discovery failed". Model and plugin requests also fail.

Sanitized log excerpts:
```text
method=account/read error={"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery failed"}
failed to refresh available models: Connection failed: error sending request
http/request send failed error_is_timeout=false error_is_connect=true
error sending request for url (https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/ps/mcp)
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use a Windows machine behind corporate HTTPS inspection and a verified PEM export of the trusted corporate root. Close all VS Code windows between launches to avoid reusing a process with the previous environment. Invoke the real code.cmd launcher, without any workaround function.

1. Open Anaconda PowerShell and activate a conda environment.
2. Set CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE to the corporate root PEM.
3. Ensure SSL_CERT_FILE points to Anaconda's Library\ssl\cacert.pem.
4. Run code.cmd . and open Codex/sign in. Observe failure.
5. Close all VS Code windows.
6. In the same Anaconda shell, run:
```powershell
Remove-Item Env:\SSL_CERT_FILE
code.cmd .
```
7. Codex now starts/connects successfully.

With CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE set, launching from ordinary PowerShell, Command Prompt, and UCRT64/MSYS2 also worked. The distinguishing tested variable was Anaconda's SSL_CERT_FILE.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should honor the explicit corporate CA configuration consistently when SSL_CERT_FILE is present for other software. The authentication documentation describes SSL_CERT_FILE as a fallback when CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE is unset:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth#custom-ca-bundles

Please investigate whether an underlying trust-store loader or separate HTTP/TLS client consumes SSL_CERT_FILE independently, whether the bundled version differs from documented behavior, or whether the documentation needs clarification. The exact internal cause has not been established.

Please also surface the underlying TLS/trust error and effective CA configuration (without credentials) instead of only a generic workspace routing failure.

### Additional information

Working mitigation: a PowerShell code wrapper temporarily removes SSL_CERT_FILE while invoking the actual code.cmd, then restores the variable in the parent shell in a finally block. Other settings, including conda activation and CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE, are retained. This works in the affected environment. No certificate verification is disabled and Anaconda's bundle is unchanged.

Anaconda's OpenSSL activation script sets SSL_CERT_FILE when initially unset. The current OpenSSL 3.5.9 package and cached older 3.0.18 package both contain this behavior; an Anaconda update introducing the setting has not been established.

An earlier corporate certificate rotation was separately detected and the exported root PEM was refreshed before the shell comparisons.

The extension is on the stable channel; the alpha suffix above comes from the bundled executable's own version output, not a switch to the pre-release extension.

Personal paths, account identifiers, credentials, and full logs have been omitted.

Enable app routing for remote curated Agent Plugins

## Why

Agent Plugin manifests previously skipped app declarations, including service-generated declarations installed with remote curated plugins. This prevented those plugins from using app routing and suppressing matching direct MCP connections.

## What changed

- Recognize app declarations for Agent Plugins from `openai-curated-remote` across loading, capability summaries, plugin details, tool suggestions, and install authentication.
- Apply app routing to suppress same-name MCP servers when an app route is available. Keep unrelated MCP servers available and preserve direct MCP access in API-key mode.
- Keep app declarations inactive for Agent Plugins from other marketplaces.

## Testing

Add coverage for marketplace and authentication routing, service-generated app declarations during installation with both manifest formats, and app tools reaching turns. Verify that disabling Apps does not restore matching direct MCP connections.

items.title: Omit reasoning and compaction from Decisions snapshot comparisons
items.body:
Omit reasoning and compaction from Decisions snapshot comparisons

## Why

Decisions snapshot comparisons reject requests containing reasoning or compaction, while conversation comparisons already omit those items. A parent compaction also causes snapshot comparisons to be rejected.

## What changed

- Share filtering of reasoning, compaction, and context compaction across both comparison modes, and ignore parent compaction when building the Decisions request.
- Distinguish malformed request setup from unsupported input items. Record setup errors as failures and unsupported input items as skipped comparisons.

## Testing

Extend the HTTP contract test to cover both comparison modes with reasoning, compaction, context compaction, and parent compaction while preserving message content. Update assertions for the distinct setup and unsupported-input errors.

items.body:
### What version of the app are you using?

ChatGPT macOS desktop app **26.1013.40934** (released October 16, 2026; “Powered by Codex & OWL”).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS desktop app.

### What issue are you seeing?

A chart generated inside a completed ChatGPT response does not render. The surrounding response text and chart heading appear normally, and the page reserves a large area for the visualization, but the chart itself is blank. No plotted line, axes, labels, legend, or usable fallback data is shown.

The response had already finished generating, so this was not just a temporary loading state. The empty chart area makes the chart-dependent part of the answer unusable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the ChatGPT macOS desktop app.
2. Ask ChatGPT to analyze time-series data and include a line chart or trend graph in the answer.
3. Wait for the response to finish completely.
4. Scroll to the generated chart section.
5. Observe that the chart container is present, but its contents are blank or almost entirely missing.

### Expected behavior

The completed response should display the full chart, including its plotted series, axes, tick labels, legend, and other required visual elements. If the interactive renderer fails, the app should provide a static image, table, or explicit error/fallback instead of silently showing an empty area.

### Actual behavior

Only an empty chart canvas is shown. The textual analysis remains visible, but the visualization cannot be read or used.

### Impact

This is a severe usability regression for research and data-analysis workflows. Important numerical results can be hidden with no visible error, and the user cannot verify or interpret the trend that the answer claims to present.

### Diagnostics

An in-app bug report was submitted with diagnostic logs.

**Feedback ID:** `c3d66717-76db-4f69-b9ba-c83d15101750`

### Additional information

The original screenshots are not attached because they contain unrelated private conversation and account UI details. A sanitized reproduction can be provided if needed.

Please investigate the chart/embedded-visualization renderer in macOS build `26.1013.40934`, including why a completed chart can fail silently without a fallback.

items.body:
## Summary

On October 20, 2026, my ChatGPT Plus five-hour Codex usage meter was exhausted unusually quickly, twice in one day, while Codex Desktop launched multiple internal `guardian_review` subagents processing near-context-limit agent histories.

October 19 was an acceptable baseline. I cannot prove from local logs whether guardian tokens are debited to the shared quota; this is a request for an engineering investigation and server-side quota attribution.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu Linux
- Client: Codex Desktop
- Plan: ChatGPT Plus
- Incident: October 20, 2026
- Local diagnostic source: Codex rollout JSONL sessions

## Observed quota progression (UTC+3)

| Time | Five-hour quota used |
|---|---:|
| 10:20 | 4% |
| 12:22 | 100% |
| 15:22 | 1% (new window) |
| 15:53 | 24% |
| 16:30 | 66% |
| 16:35 | 77% |
| 16:45 | 94% |

These values come from `event_msg.token_count.rate_limits.primary.used_percent`. They are snapshots of rolling five-hour windows, not per-request charges.

## Evidence from rollout logs

- 11 October 20 session files have `source.subagent.other = "guardian"`, `thread_source = "guardian_review"`, `originator = "Codex Desktop"`.
- Guardian's developer prompt explicitly asks it to judge the risk and authorization of a planned coding-agent action.
- Individual safety-review user inputs replay approximately **200,000–312,000 characters** of agent history. Some include `guardian_context_omission`.
- One guardian session reports two responses of **241,777** and **243,180** input tokens against a **258,400** context window. The second response reports **241,536 cached input tokens**.
- October 20 files contain **14 `turn_aborted` events**, each marked `interrupted`, versus two in the October 19 files.
- Several guardian sessions have identical serialized compaction hashes and the same parent thread, consistent with reusing/restoring the same compacted history.
- The largest review histories are associated with a long-running coding thread. I am withholding project paths and the raw transcripts to avoid disclosing private data.

The logs do not provide a complete breakdown of the account's quota debit between primary model work and internal reviews. They establish unusually heavy safety-review inputs occurring during the reported fast-depletion period.

## Expected behavior

Safety review should remain effective without unnecessarily replaying almost the entire agent history for each action. Internal review activity and its effect (if any) on user quota should be reasonably transparent.

## Investigation requested

1. Do internal `guardian_review` / auto-review model calls consume the user's Codex Plus five-hour and weekly limits?
2. If so, how much of the October 20 account usage was due to these reviews compared with the main model?
3. Why do individual reviews receive ~240k input tokens? Is context trimming, incremental review or cache reuse working as intended?
4. Are interrupted / resumed reviews resulting in redundant work or quota charges?
5. Is this a regression in Codex Desktop or its review runtime?
6. If unintended overhead affected quota, is remediation or quota correction possible?

I have separately submitted a private support request for an account-specific quota audit. Redacted telemetry can be supplied if helpful. Please use a secure channel if full JSONL files are needed, as these contain proprietary session content.

## Related

- #49572 — another report of increased auto-review/guardian traffic and quota consumption, on Windows. This Linux incident appears related but has a distinct date, usage pattern and interruption evidence.

items.title: Browser runtime leaves delayed iframe Document responses paused after CUA execution ends

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.31256 (build 20586; installed com.openai.codex application metadata)

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected; minimal reproduction requires no website account or subscription-specific service

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon; uname -mprs: Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Reporting a browser/Node REPL execution-lifetime defect with an account-free localhost reproduction, a failing installed-source regression, and a candidate source patch. Please route to the browser-desktop / Node REPL runtime owner.

A parent page renders, but its delayed, plain, same-origin iframe remains about:blank after the originating CUA invocation returns. The server sends HTTP 200 after 1.5 seconds; the parent still reports FAIL after 10 seconds. Keeping that same originating CUA invocation active for 2.5 seconds instead produces PASS and the actual child heading. This blocks reliable first-load MCP Apps acceptance through browser automation.

The minimized reproduction has no Uno services, Kit fetches, Cloudflare, OAuth, external HTTPS requests, sandbox attribute, or shared account cookies. Native Chrome loading succeeded in earlier controlled comparisons. Ordinary Node timers also ran outside the tool invocation, so a generally suspended Node event loop is not established.

**Installed-source regression:** late response handling raises `node_repl exec context not found`, never dispatches `Fetch.continueResponse`, and retains the owned paused response. Active handling succeeds. The linked harness drives real installed methods with mocked host/provider boundaries; it does not merely reimplement the suspected logic.

**Mechanism supported by source and regression:** retained AsyncLocalStorage metadata is classified as live by browser client `Kc.getSessionParams()`. Its live extension path rereads request-header requirements. The privileged bridge correctly rejects that expired execution. Response handler `qf` suppresses the rejected event-handler promise, leaving the document paused. The exact swallowed error was captured in the source harness, not directly from the live trusted worker; the source regression and live timing differential are separate evidence.

Installed input versions: `@oai/browser-desktop` 0.1.1; `@oai/cua` 0.2.6. The desktop bundle is named ChatGPT.app but identifies as `com.openai.codex`. Browser at submission: Chrome 155.0.8059.85; ChatGPT Chrome extension version observed during investigation: 1.26.1005.11759. Input hashes and timestamped localhost evidence are in the linked bundle. No installed application files were patched.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Download the plain sources from [the reproduction and candidate patch bundle](https://gist.github.com/christopherwxyz/892d1aaa5bfad78fae22c7dd68f9ebcd), or decode its original ZIP (instructions and SHA-256 are included). Start the dependency-free server:

```sh
node localhost-repro.mjs
```

2. In the existing authorized CUA Chrome session, create a test tab using the printed loopback URL. The page embeds `/child`, delayed by 1.5 seconds. The parent checks the real child heading, so about:blank cannot falsely pass.
3. In one CUA invocation, navigate/reload and take an immediate AX snapshot. Let this invocation return before the delayed response arrives.
4. Wait at least 10 seconds outside CUA, then inspect the page in a later invocation. Actual result: FAIL and a blank child, despite the server response.
5. Differential control: reload the identical page, but keep that originating CUA invocation active for 2.5 seconds, then inspect it. Actual result: PASS and `Delayed child loaded`. This is a timing control, not the proposed fix.

Representative calls after binding the test tab:

```js
// Failing arm: this invocation returns before the response.
await tab.reload();
await tab.getAXState();
```

Wait outside CUA. Inspect in another invocation.

```js
// Passing timing control, in ONE originating invocation.
await tab.reload();
await tab.getAXState();
await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2500));
await tab.getAXState();
```

Offline source regression (Node.js + Acorn + matching installed macOS application):

```sh
ACORN_PATH=/absolute/path/to/node_modules/acorn node regression.cjs
# RED, exit 1: node_repl exec context not found; response remains paused.

ACORN_PATH=/absolute/path/to/node_modules/acorn node regression.cjs --candidate
# GREEN, exit 0: exact-owner late continuation; policy and isolation guards retained.
```

The harness reads installed source and embedded functions into temporary copies, then removes those copies on exit. It never writes installed runtime files or connects to an account. Exact transformation seams fail on source drift. See README.md for full instructions.

### What is the expected behavior?

An intercepted document belonging to a still-authorized browser session/turn/target should finish its first load even if the CUA invocation that initiated navigation has returned. Expired execution metadata must not be treated as permission to perform privileged configuration operations. A late callback must never borrow a newer session/turn's cached authority. Revoked targets must remain denied and receive appropriate provider-owned lifecycle cleanup. Errors should not silently strand a paused navigation.

### Additional information

### Candidate patch and regression coverage

`candidate.cjs` is an executable, guarded source-transformation proposal for the observed installed version, not a binary patch or an upstream Git commit. No external PR is being proposed, consistent with the contributing guide.

The proposal adds an explicit execution-active predicate through the trusted context/bridge and worker factory, forwards it explicitly through browser factory `Aae`, and wires both normal and Dot clients. Originating request metadata remains intact. Inactive callbacks can select cached context only when the cached session and turn exactly match that originating metadata; mismatches fail closed. Active executions still refresh policy, and inactive privileged config access remains denied. Existing no-context cached parameter selection is preserved.

The source harness exercises real context, privileged bridge/worker factory, browser factory, client constructors, and response handler. Host transport initialization and provider responses are mocked. It covers active policy refresh, late same-owner continuation, newer-owner rejection for both same-session/new-turn and cross-session while another execution runs and after it ends, privileged denial, released/revoked provider denial, no-context cached parameters, and the Dot access assertion path with mocked info. Independent review found no blocking defects in the final proposal.

**Limits:** real-provider acceptance of the candidate, the complete Dot lifecycle, and provider-side disposal after denied continuation remain unverified. Denied responses remain marked owned in the harness. No rebuilt runtime or production first-load fix has been verified. Please do not treat a passing source-copy test as shipping acceptance.

### Patch, tests, and reproduction evidence

**Published bundle:** https://gist.github.com/christopherwxyz/892d1aaa5bfad78fae22c7dd68f9ebcd

All source files and red/green outputs are directly available as text. The exact original ZIP, including both PNG screenshots, is provided as `uno-browser-runtime-fix.zip.b64`, with decoding instructions in `DOWNLOAD.md`.

The linked ZIP contains all patch/test/reproduction sources, full red/green outputs, versions and SHA-256 hashes, sanitized timestamped localhost events, and paired failure/control screenshots. ZIP SHA-256: `eff0c183598584a22985b8579ef1d7dadaf2581f9689a6de488e8f4b84398009`. No credentials, private account identifiers, production content, or personal filesystem paths are included.

### Related reports and acceptance gate

Related but not established as the same defect: #37013 concerns Windows helper context reuse across executions; commenters report a Windows helper update fixed that path. This report concerns macOS browser-managed Fetch Document response completion after the originating invocation ends. #21144 concerns iframe inspection/input, whereas the minimized iframe here is plain and same-origin and never finishes loading. Exact `Fetch.continueResponse`/`requestPaused` searches found no matching report.

Downstream UNO-607 remains open. Acceptance requires a fixed runtime to pass the localhost test across separate completed CUA invocations, then render the production Uno MCP Apps iframe on first load under strict CSP, without Try again. No new account, consent, payment, Kit write, or CSP relaxation is required for that retest.

# OpenAI report: embedded MCP App first launch stalls with Browser Control attached

Updated 2026-10-20 for submission. No private transcript, screenshots, cookies,
headers, OAuth values, signed media links, or raw logs are included.

## Latest reproduction with deployed diagnostics

The diagnostic instrumentation is now deployed, not merely tested locally:

- Commit: `3aa5d5cfe3015871e6244c8e1261fe7213ffd0ae`.
- Serving revision at verification: `figma-animator-r3aa5d5cfe301-0199c16e7c38`, 100% traffic.

`figma_media_browser({})` launch was requested, without a previous `uiSessionId`.
Browser Control remained attached. No Try again, debugger detachment, forced
continuation, or guard changes were used. The panel stayed blank and ChatGPT
displayed `Couldn’t display Figma Animator MCP`.

The server recorded `mcp.ui.launch.requested` at `17:29:25.331 UTC`:

```json
{

the correlated server event in a follow-up requesting only the status tool.

{

  "evidence": "none",
  "launchId": "dd3bc0d6-d68c-4b8d-8bc5-c2529899a909",
  "bundleId": "f6ea57a1bac598777b461ba1f3eb6546d605b953b99da722ec8575a80689f2b8"
}
```

No rendering event or acknowledgment-tool invocation appeared in the
revision-scoped log query covering this launch. The viewer was closed only after
saving blank-panel evidence, to read the conversation in the narrow layout. It
was not reopened. The status query did not launch or retry the UI.

The supported debugger cursor was captured before launch. The bounded filtered
trace was not truncated and captured a sandbox-origin `Fetch.requestPaused`,
resource type Document, HTTP 200, event sequence 504, request
`interception-job-15837.0`. It also captured an earlier OpenAI CDN Document pause.
This is not a complete network trace and does not expose continuation completion.

The live status verifies the absence of a client acknowledgment for this launch;
it does not by itself identify a bridge root cause. The visible host failure card
is separate evidence of the failed panel launch.

## Summary

A fresh ChatGPT web Figma Animator panel launch fails while the official Chrome
Browser Control connection remains attached. A supported debugger event read
captures an HTTP 200 HTML Document response from the ChatGPT web-sandbox origin.
The panel later displays `Couldn’t display Figma Animator MCP`. A supported
`Page.getFrameTree` request is refused because Browser Use is resolving a paused
document response. The actual internal continuation outcome is unavailable.

## Environment

- macOS; Google Chrome through the official extension-backed Browser Control.
- Desktop app: 26.1013.40934, build 20770, production channel.
- Official desktop updater reported `up_to_date` on 2026-10-20.
- Bundled browser plugin: 26.1013.40934.
- Latest backend/UI revision tested: `3aa5d5cfe3015871e6244c8e1261fe7213ffd0ae`.
- Existing app: `asdk_app_6ad28c02de6c8191a5e5476c13f0edd7`.
- Endpoint: `https://figma.meds-marketing.dev/mcp`; existing BlueChew audience.
- Installed Chrome and extension versions were not re-collected for this
  reproduction; please collect them in any internal reproduction.

## Minimal steps

1. Use an authorized account with the existing Figma Animator MCP connection.
2. Keep official Browser Control attached throughout.
3. In a new ChatGPT chat, request:

   > Use the existing Figma Animator MCP app to call figma_media_browser with {}
   > and open its browser UI. This is a read-only fresh-launch test. Do not
   > generate media, reuse a uiSessionId, or retry a failed UI launch.

4. Observe the panel, and use the supported CDP event reader to inspect
   `Fetch.requestPaused`. For a new capture, obtain a cursor before step 3,
   page to completion, and record any truncation.
5. After the stalled launch, request `Page.getFrameTree` through the supported
   tab CDP capability. Do not force continuation or change interception.

Expected: the panel mounts and displays its Figma browser on the first attempt
while Browser Control remains attached.

Observed: blank panel followed by the host failure card. No Try again,
debugger detach, forced request continuation, or guard changes were used.

## Earlier reproduction and guard evidence

Reproduction captured on 2026-10-20, approximately 16:35–16:37 UTC:

- Event sequence 279: `Fetch.requestPaused`, `resourceType: Document`,
  `responseStatusCode: 200`, `content-type: text/html`, `content-encoding: br`.
- Origin: ChatGPT `web-sandbox.oaiusercontent.com`; query/fragment omitted.
- Request correlation: `interception-job-12963.0` (local debugger identifier).
- Filtered event page was not truncated. This is not a complete network trace.
- Supported query returned exactly:
  `Raw CDP is unavailable while Browser Use is resolving a paused document response.`
- Screenshot retained privately; not attached because it includes workspace context.
- All 20 current-day desktop log files under the officially documented macOS
  log directory were searched. No continuation method, guard, or matching request
  entries were found. IAB route warnings do not establish this Chrome failure's cause.

The assistant reported successful display despite the host failure card. Its
text is not rendering evidence. The earlier test used revision
`656081dd815fe7e161d827c534cd40a85e7c03c3`, before acknowledgment instrumentation.
The latest deployed reproduction above supplies the new evidence.

## Investigation requested

Please correlate the active owned-document set at the guard rejection with:

1. The exact paused request and frame/target/session ownership.
2. Continuation start, completion, rejection, timeout, or a handler that never
   reached continuation.
3. The safe method/error classification and terminal request state.
4. The corresponding ownership release or retention decision.

Please provide a supported diagnostic build/API or a fixed release retaining
the document guard. Do not unblock raw CDP around an unresolved document.

Static inspection and an isolated mock show that the bundled handler can suppress
a rejection and retain ownership. They do **not** establish that this live request
rejected, or prove a common root cause with other reports.

Related upstream report: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55166

Official escalation guidance:
https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/troubleshooting

## Deployed application instrumentation

Each UI-producing tool response carries `uiLaunch` with a random launch ID,
bundle SHA-256 and `awaiting_render_ack`. An app-only callback can acknowledge a
nonhidden, nonzero app layout after two animation frames. A read-only status tool
returns the receipt or leaves rendering unverified. This distinguishes mounted
app evidence from tool success; it does not prove preview images loaded or replace
independent visual verification. No application code can acknowledge a sandbox
document that never starts the app's JavaScript.
